issue.title: f32 residual-VQ store + mul-free graded-signature query assignment (#230 follow-up: accuracy / address-space design)
issue.body:
### Summary
Follow-up to #230, accuracy half — and an **address-space design decision**, not a local performance patch. The A-binary vs A-f32 gap (3.9pp top-1, 4.5pp agreement) is inherent to sign-only 1-bit thresholding reused unchanged across stages, vs the f32 ablation's L2-normalized true residual-VQ (`certify.rs:220-262`: per-stage nearest-centroid with residual subtraction).

### Key enabler
`INFERENCE_OPERATION_CONTRACT.md` §4: *"Compilation and training are explicitly unrestricted by this contract."* The store may legally be built with f32 residual-VQ assignment; only the **query side** must stay mul-free.

### Candidate designs (benchmark both)
1. **Integer residual subtraction**: ship quantized copies of the `ctx_cb` centroids (already exist compiler-side, `compiler.rs:686-689`, currently never serialized); per stage: subtract in the integer kernel (add/sub/shift all permitted), re-threshold with per-stage thresholds. Recovers the residual-VQ structure — the main mathematical gap.
2. **Multi-bit graded signatures**: quantize per-dimension *magnitude* (2-4 bits, not just sign) against per-stage thresholds, compare by popcount. Normalization folds into offline threshold derivation. This applies the geometric-coordinate method (hypersphere magnitudes) to the primary engine's addressing.

### Address-space framing (review requirement)
The quantization scheme **is** the address space: it decides collision structure, cacheability, and what "nearby" means for any future distributed/content-addressed serving of store regions. Sign-thresholding is an LSH of the bundle space — Hamming neighborhood = semantic neighborhood is a designed property to preserve. Review quantization choices as UOR addressing decisions, not kernel micro-optimizations.

### DoD
- Recover ≥ half the A-f32 gap (target: ≥30.1% top-1, ≥34.1% agreement) at unchanged runtime op census — P-4 machine-checked scan stays green (no multiply/divide/float in the deployed kernel).
- Store-region κ-compatibility documented: identical pinned inputs ⇒ identical signatures ⇒ identical region addresses across platforms (determinism invariant extended to the new assignment path).
- Measured on Maura's `certify` harness (#230's built-in control).

*Blocked for trustworthy HF-path measurement by #242. Interacts with the store-size decision (#243).*

comments.body:
## Phase A implementation plan (sign-off recorded in the doc, PR #270; baseline: the completed #244 matrix)

Certifier-side decomposition rows (docs/graded_signature_address_design.md §Phase A), each isolating one loss in the A-f32→A-binary gap (32.1/36.4 → 28.2/31.9), measured on the D3 artifacts with the existing harness (artifact κ-reuse + bounded stages per the #244 methodology):

- **A-norm-only** — f32 assignment with only the normalization replaced by the runtime's threshold/sign path.
- **A-resid-only** — f32 first-stage, runtime residual handling thereafter.
- **A-G(b)** — thermometer-graded signatures, b∈{2,3,4} (Hamming=L1 order-preserving).
- **A-R** — integer residual subtraction (doc's risk note re class_sigs retraining in residual space applies).
- **A-R∘G** — composed.

**Exit rule** (from the doc): a single-loss row recovering ≥~70% of the gap ⇒ minimal fix ships, remaining designs close as not-needed. **Empirical criterion**: ≥30.1% top1 / ≥34.1% agreement at unchanged op census (multiply=0). Rows land as certifier code first (one PR), then a bounded measurement run on the Mac (~25-40 min per the artifact-reuse pattern), results posted here, then the ship decision per the doc's decision box. Post-#281 note: rows measure against the single-key+query-beam shipped semantics (A row), with A-multi retained for continuity.

## Phase A decomposition table — measured (2026-07-29, D3 harness, fresh compile, artifact κ blake3:81db44…)

Baselines: floor A-single 27.0/30.5 · shipped A (query-beam) 28.2/31.9 · ceiling A-f32 32.1/36.4. Gap floor→ceiling: 5.1pp top1 / 5.9pp agreement.

| Row | top1 | agree | WB | keys | gap recovered (top1/agree) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-norm-only (sign-unit Euclidean, no residuals) | 29.5 | 33.4 | 10.1631 | 87,129 | 49% / 49% |
| **A-resid-only (raw-space residual VQ)** | **30.3** | **33.9** | **9.6940** | **49,048** | **65% / 58%** |
| A-G(2) | 28.0 | 31.6 | 10.2159 | 108,603 | 20% / 19% |
| A-G(3) | 28.1 | 31.9 | 10.1881 | 108,584 | 22% / 24% |
| A-G(4) | 28.8 | 32.7 | 10.0661 | 105,660 | 35% / 37% |
| A-R (buildable: unretrained class_sigs) | 27.0 | 30.5 | 9.7667 | 183,459 | **0% / 0%** |
| A-R∘G(2) | 29.3 | 33.1 | 9.9814 | 123,088 | 45% / 44% |
| A-R∘G(3) | 29.2 | 33.1 | 9.8906 | 133,202 | 43% / 44% |
| A-R∘G(4) | 29.4 | 33.4 | 9.9079 | 118,276 | 47% / 49% |

## Reading

1. **Residuals are the dominant loss** — A-resid-only recovers ~60-65% of the gap alone, with the FEWEST keys of any row (49k, 2.7× below the shipped store) and the best WB in the entire matrix including the ceiling's neighborhood (9.694 vs shipped 9.874). Loss #1 ≫ losses #2/#3, answering the doc's Phase-B ordering question.
2. **Exit rule (≥70% single-loss ⇒ minimal fix): not triggered** — 65% is close but under. **Criterion (≥30.1/≥34.1): no row passes both** — A-resid-only passes top1 (30.3) and misses agreement by 0.2pp.
3. **The doc's Design-R risk note is confirmed empirically**: A-R with unretrained class_sigs recovers exactly 0% — sign re-thresholding of residuals against original-space prototypes is worthless. Grading partially rescues it (R∘G ~47%) because quantile ladders adapt to residual distributions where class_sigs cannot.
4. **Recommendation for Phase B**: Design R with class_sigs retrained in residual space (compile-side, contract §4 permits it) is the path — the f32 residual signal is real and cheap (49k keys), and the ⚑ R-vs-G decision resolves to **R (with retrained per-stage prototypes), G(4) grading optional as composition**. If retraining closes the remaining 0.2pp agreement shortfall, the criterion is met.

Rows merged in PR #286; run log /tmp/i243-phasea2.log (Casey's Mac). Caveats recorded inline in the row labels (G-prototype grading is lower-bound instrumentation).

## Phase B decision rows, rounds 1-2 (2026-07-29 evening, D3 harness, fresh compile, corpus 150k/754 stories/30,036 held-out — same recipe as the Phase A table)

**Round 1 — negative result, recorded:** an A-R-retrained row (prototypes = residual-space centroid sign-signatures) measured **bit-identical** to A-R (27.0/30.5, WB 9.7667, 183,459 keys). Cause, by code reading after the fact: `class_sigs` already ARE the centroid sign-signatures (compiler.rs packs `cb > 0.0` per stage). Prototype retraining at the sign level does not exist as a degree of freedom — the design doc's Design-R risk note pointed at a distinction that is empty at this layer.

**Round 2 — the metric-isolation rows split the hypothesis, decisively:**

| Row | top1 | agree | WB | keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-resid-only (Phase A, f32 Euclid + subtraction) | 30.3 | 33.9 | 9.6940 | 49,048 |
| **A-dot-only (dot assignment, NO subtraction)** | **30.4** | **34.2** | **9.6342** | **47,603** |
| A-resid-sign (sign-Hamming + the same subtraction) | 27.0 | 30.5 | 10.2311 | 134,762 |
| A-single / A-R (floor) | 27.0 | 30.5 | — | — |

## Revised reading (supersedes the Phase A attribution)

1. **The dominant loss is the assignment metric, not residual wiring.** A-dot-only reproduces and slightly beats A-resid-only with zero residual updates; A-resid-sign — residuals present, sign metric — collapses exactly to the floor. Mechanism: `centered` bundles are raw-scale while `ctx_cb` is unit-scale, so A-resid-only's Euclidean argmin was `argmax dot(work, cent)` in disguise and its subtraction was numerically negligible. The Phase A rows measured this without isolating it.
2. **A-dot-only passes the Empirical Criterion outright** (30.4 ≥ 30.1, 34.2 ≥ 34.1) with the best WB in the entire matrix (9.6342 < A-f32's 9.6982) and the fewest keys (47.6k = 7.2× under the shipped store). That is the instrumentation ceiling for any mul-free dot approximation.
3. **Phase B target pivots**: not residual-VQ kernel wiring — a **shift-add dot**: centroid entries restricted to (sums of) signed powers of two turn `dot(work, cent)` into a shift-and-add reduction over the integer work vector. Contract §4 holds — shifts and integer adds, no multiply op. Buildability rows (A-dot-po2 one-term, A-dot-po2x2 two-term) are in the round-3 run now; if either holds ≥30.1/≥34.1, the kernel design is settled.

Consequences noted for the doc's decision box: Design R closes as not-the-mechanism (its measured 65% was not residuals); Design G's grading remains a candidate encoding of the SAME dot approximation (thermometer L1 as a coarse dot) rather than an independent design; #276's P row inherits the corrected baseline. Full logs: /tmp/i243-phaseb-certify.log, /tmp/i243-round2-certify.log (Casey's Mac); rows land with the batch-2 branch.

## Round 3 — buildability verdict: PASS. Phase B kernel design is settled.

| Row | top1 | agree | WB | keys | criterion (≥30.1 / ≥34.1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A-dot-only (f32 ceiling) | 30.4 | 34.2 | 9.6342 | 47,603 | pass |
| **A-dot-po2 (1-term ±2^s centroids)** | **30.6** | **34.2** | **9.6269** | 48,307 | **pass** |
| **A-dot-po2x2 (2-term)** | **30.7** | **34.3** | 9.6373 | **47,418** | **pass** |

The power-of-two value-set restriction costs **nothing** — both buildable rows match or beat the f32 dot ceiling on every metric (the crude quantization acts as mild regularization). The store lands at ~47-48k keys, 7.2× under the shipped store, with the best WB figures in the whole decomposition matrix.

## Decision (per the doc's decision box, measurement-made)

**Phase B implements shift-add dot assignment**: per stage, argmax over K=256 of Σ_d ±(work[d] << s_{k,d}) with centroid entries compiled to signed powers of two (⚑ 1-term vs 2-term: 2-term is marginally better on all three metrics — pick at kernel-implementation time; both pass). Runtime ops: shifts + integer adds + compares — contract §4 holds, no multiply op, no float. Residual wiring is dead (round 2: contributes nothing in sign space, and the dot rows need no subtraction at all); Design R closes as not-the-mechanism; Design G survives only as an encoding question inside the dot approximation, not as an independent design.

Kernel work (artifact-versioned format bump for the po2 centroid tables, P-4 source-scan extension, kernel-vs-plain equality witness) is the next #243 PR — individual PR per the process amendment, since it touches the runtime kernel. Then Phase C adoption + κ re-pin with era note, which also delivers #230 (the 3.71× fragmentation resolves to ~47k keys with higher accuracy).

Rows and logs: batch-2 branch (3 commits), /tmp/i243-{phaseb,round2,round3}-certify.log on Casey's Mac. Corpus: gen 300 150000 recipe, 150k tokens / 754 stories / 30,036 held-out — same as the Phase A table.

## Phase B kernel: shipped for review — PR #291. Integer semantics confirmed, criterion passed, and one correction to the record.

**Final integer-kernel table** (run 4, metric-consistent; full evidence in the PR):

| Row | top1 | agree | WB | keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OLD shipped (sign + beam) | 28.2 | 31.9 | 9.7868 | 134,733 |
| **NEW shipped (shift-add dot + beam)** | **30.7** | **34.3** | **9.0242** | **47,476** |
| NEW primary-key only | 30.6 | 34.2 | 9.6389 | 47,476 |

Criterion (≥30.1/≥34.1): **pass** on real kernel arithmetic — truncating arithmetic shifts cost nothing vs the f32 emulation. Witnesses clean, multiply 0.

**Correction to my run-1/2 comments above**: the 18.3/20.6 beam row was NOT a beam defect and NOT the dot metric — `eval_query_beam` was deriving sign-metric membership prefixes and probing a dot-keyed store (key-space mismatch). With memberships from the same metric that keys the store, **the beam helps** (+0.1pp both metrics and a 0.6-bit WB improvement over primary-key-only), so the #244 beam decision shape stands unchanged under dot. Two certify runs were wasted on the misdiagnosis before the code-path check that settled it — recorded per the measurement-discipline rule now in force (verify the diff is in the measured path before spending a run).

**⚑ open at PR review**: op budget (~13× the sign path's adds/shifts; mitigations queued: 1-term tables, stage early-exit, #277 VP-tree) and the A-multi ablation row's metric-inconsistency note.

**Next per phasing**: PR #291 through the queue → Phase C adoption decision (TLA6 default = κ re-pin with era note, maintainer call; serving/score signature-path adoption; BASELINE table; closes #230).

Phase B kernel landed: merge dcb1eb6582aaeccae941a60288be36e1884ecd3d (PR #291; queue unblocked by #292, f069c4a0fe3cb525adb224f90f8aaf73fd7c3abf). Shipped integer semantics: shift-add dot + metric-consistent beam — **30.7/34.3, WB 9.0242, 47,476 keys, multiply 0** (vs 28.2/31.9 / 9.7868 / 134,733 shipped before). Next: **Phase C adoption** — TLA6 default emission (κ re-pin + era note, maintainer decision for Casey), serving/score signature-path adoption, BASELINE table; closes #230 on completion. ⚑ op-budget mitigations (1-term tables, stage early-exit, #277 VP-tree) open on the PR record.

**Maintainer decision (Casey, 2026-07-29): Phase C proceeds with a κ re-pin now, and the default emission is 1-term TLA6.**

Rationale on the record: the 1-term dot tables measured equal accuracy to 13-term (PR #291 mitigation record), so adopting 1-term as the default resolves the ⚑ 13× per-token op-budget increase *before* the pin instead of mitigating it after. Term count had to be decided pre-pin — changing it later is a second re-pin. Single κ re-pin with a TLA5 era note in the proof/baseline record; #265 (canonical deterministic compile) is explicitly *not* bundled in and will re-pin in its own era when it lands.

Phase C work order: (1) 1-term TLA6 default emission + κ re-pin + era note, (2) serving/score signature-path adoption (R4Engine + score.r4g1 replay are sig-only today) with its own evidence run, (3) BASELINE table. Closes #230 on completion.

⚑ **Composition finding (pre-merge queue simulation, 2026-07-30): 1-term TLA6 fixture × #234 full-code-only Rule 2 collapses fixture exact-context coverage.** Local merge of main + PR #294 + PR #296, trend harness run: strict EXCT-miss 99.03%, status split ExactContext 291 / Graph 29,725 / Novel 20, rule12 1.11%/15.97 bits (graph per-status 0.84%/16.03); the TLA3-baseline row on the dot-path store reads 22.98%/9.51 (bits improve 12.36→9.51, agreement drops 30.0→23.0). Mechanism: dot assignment yields a finer, more diverse code space (48,321 single-write keys), so held-out full codes almost never coincide with train full codes — strict exact-context recall evaporates and everything routes to the still-weak graph path.

Consequences on the record: (1) PR #296 will carry the corresponding trend re-pin (era note) and is sequenced AFTER #294 in the queue; (2) for Phase C serving/score adoption, TLA6-compiled bundles under strict EXCT will mostly resolve Graph/Novel → D4 abstention — the C serving row will read very differently, which is the adoption evidence run's job to measure, not a surprise; (3) this sharpens the #234 conclusion: the graph path (0.84% here) is now unambiguously the load-bearing number to improve, and #277 (VP-tree) / #246 (design-matrix) style retrieval work is what moves it. Caught by a local queue simulation before burning a merge-group cycle — both failed orders were reproduced offline.

**Phase C part 1 COMPLETE** (merge f6314aa, PR #296): 1-term TLA6 default emission (`DOT_TERMS=1`), κ re-pinned (3rd era: only the container pin moved, 462,092→1,051,916 bytes, blake3:81db4406…→cf64fe74…; all non-container κs byte-identical — verified by dump), era notes in baseline_kappa.json + PROOF.md P5(a), trend pin priced at the combined honest row. Decision row on the census-verified binary: **A 30.5/34.0, WB 9.0107 (better than 2-term 9.0242), 48,321 keys, op census halved (add 317,850 / shift 317,502)** — the PR #291 ⚑ op-budget flag is resolved. Bonus catch: the TLA6 fixture exposed and fixed a writer/reader metric inconsistency in `index_token_stream` (sig-path writes, dot-path reads).

**Part 2 scoping (sig-path adoption) — design fork found, maintainer input needed before authoring:** the score surface (cover regions, memberships, witness replay) is signature-keyed end-to-end, and the dot metric needs the integer bundle, which `ScoreWitness` does not carry and the 288-bit sig cannot reconstruct. The EXCT probe inside `score_runtime` does `assign_plain(art, sig)` (sign codes) while a TLA6 bundle's runtime store is dot-keyed — the same class of inconsistency as the tless indexer, but fixing it touches the witness contract. Options: (A) witness carries the 4-byte graded code — serving assigns via dot, replay verifies consumption of the attested code, code *derivation* stays proven at certify time (kernel==plain equality witnesses); (B) witness carries the full integer bundle — replay re-derives everything, witness grows ~2.3 KB/prediction; (C) score.r4g1 emission stays sign-keyed under TLA6 — witness contract untouched, metric unification deferred, C row measures a sign-keyed serving surface. ⚑ Casey.

**Maintainer decision (Casey, 2026-07-30): Part 2 takes option A — the ScoreWitness carries the 4-byte graded code.** Serving assigns via the artifact's declared metric from the live bundle; replay verifies consumption of the attested code; code derivation remains proven at certify time by the kernel==plain equality witnesses. Witness schema bumps accordingly. Authoring begins on a fresh branch off f6314aa; C-row evidence run (TLA6-recompiled D3 bundle) follows the code.

**Composition finding corrected (part 2 measurement, PR #298):** the 1.11%/15.97 fixture collapse was NOT primarily the finer dot code space — it was the writer/reader mismatch itself (sign-code probes against the dot-keyed store, measured pre-adoption). With witness-attested metric-consistent codes: **rule12 31.63%/9.1181 — the best fixture row on record** (sign-era tie: 30.02/10.24) — status split ExactContext 25,853 / Graph 4,182 / Novel 1, strict miss 13.93% (Gate C valid AND the graph path exercised on real probes), baseline on the dot store 33.83%/11.95. The dot metric under strict EXCT is a strict improvement once probed consistently. Trend re-pin travels in PR #298 (first live use of the #297 self-consistency mode). C-row evidence pair on the TLA6 D3 bundle is running; BASELINE table + #230 close after it lands.

Closing the epic — decided, built, measured, merged, pinned:

**Phase A** (#286): decomposition rows attributing the A-f32→A-binary gap. **Phase B** (#291, dcb1eb6): shift-add dot kernel, 30.7/34.3, WB 9.0242, 47,476 keys, multiply 0. **Phase C part 1** (#296, f6314aa): 1-term TLA6 default emission (maintainer decision 2026-07-29), κ re-pin era 3 (container-only move, blake3:cf64fe74…), op census halved (317,850/317,502) resolving the #291 ⚑, A row 30.5/34.0 WB 9.0107. **Phase C part 2** (#298, 97495db): witness-attested graded codes (option A, maintainer decision 2026-07-30), coded scorer/step surfaces, metric-consistent harness; fixture row 31.63%/9.1181 (best on record), D3 row 5.38/15.22 beating same-corpus baseline on both metrics for the first time, strict miss ~13.7% on both distributions (Gate C valid). Trend pins re-priced with era notes at every step; three latent writer/reader metric inconsistencies found and fixed along the way (tless indexer, EXCT probe, harness baseline).

Deferred to #299 (mechanical, non-blocking): the TLA6 C serving row under relative_tla + a C-only certify mode. BASELINE table refresh rides the next docs touch. #230 closed on this evidence; the graph path is the measured number to improve next (#277/#246).
